visual: Bushy evergreen shrub prized for dramatic fiery red young foliage, which matures through coppery-green to glossy dark green. Branched clusters of creamy-white, urn-shaped flowers appear in mid spring.
water: Keep consistently moist during establishment. Established plants prefer reliable moisture but should never remain waterlogged.
aspect: Full sun to partial shade; sheltered east-, south- or west-facing position
soil: Moderately fertile, humus-rich, acidic, moist but well-drained soil. Use ericaceous compost when container grown.
soilWarning: Requires acidic soil. Avoid alkaline or chalky conditions, which can cause nutrient deficiency and yellowing foliage. Avoid waterlogging.
prune: Requires little routine pruning. Remove dead, damaged or unwanted growth after flowering and lightly shape if necessary.
toxicity: Harmful if eaten. Harmful to pets if eaten. Wear gloves and protective equipment when handling.
hardinessNote: Hardy in most places throughout the UK, approximately -15 to -10°C. Young plants may benefit from winter protection.
resilience: Hardy and long-lived in suitable acidic soil, though vulnerable to poor drainage and unsuitable alkaline conditions.
uses: Ericaceous borders, woodland gardens, cottage gardens, courtyard gardens, mixed shrub borders and containers.
foliage: Evergreen; young leaves emerge brilliant red, mature through coppery-green and eventually become dark glossy green.
container: Well suited to large containers using ericaceous compost, particularly where garden soil is alkaline.
